title: Gluten-Free Cinnamon Brown Sugar Cupcakes
shortDescription: Gluten-free cinnamon brown sugar cupcakes take 25 minutes to prep and 18 minutes to bake.
description: These cupcakes taste like a cinnamon roll in cake form. The batter uses brown sugar and a good pinch of cinnamon, so the crumb stays soft and moist even without gluten. I tested this recipe three times in my own kitchen before I got the texture right. The trick is a gluten-free flour blend with xanthan gum already mixed in, plus sour cream for extra moisture. The frosting is a simple vanilla buttercream swirled with a cinnamon sugar ribbon, then dusted with more cinnamon on top. It looks fancy but takes ten minutes to make. These are great for fall gatherings, but honestly I make them all year. Nobody guesses they are gluten-free until you tell them.
ingredients: 1 3/4 cups gluten-free all-purpose flour blend (with xanthan gum)
2 tbsp brown sugar mixed with 1/2 tsp cinnamon (for swirl)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk the gluten-free flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt in a bowl.
Beat 1/2 cup butter and brown sugar until fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, then mix in vanilla and sour cream.
Add the dry mix in two batches, alternating with the milk. Mix just until smooth.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two-thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a rack.
Beat 1 1/2 cups butter until smooth. Add powdered sugar in batches, then vanilla and heavy cream.
Swirl the brown sugar cinnamon mix into the frosting with a few gentle folds, do not overmix.
Pipe frosting onto cooled cupcakes and dust each one with cinnamon before serving.
tips: Use a gluten-free flour blend that already has xanthan gum, so you don't need to add more.
Let the batter rest 5 minutes before baking. This helps gluten-free flour absorb the liquid.
Fold the cinnamon sugar into the frosting gently so you get streaks, not a solid brown color.
Store leftovers in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days.

faq.question: Can I use a different gluten-free flour blend?
faq.answer: Yes, but check that it has xanthan gum listed. Blends without it can make the cupcakes crumbly.

faq.question: Why did my gluten-free cupcakes sink in the middle?
faq.answer: This usually means the oven was too cool or the pan was opened too early. Check your oven temperature with a thermometer and wait until at least 15 minutes to peek.

faq.question: Can I make these dairy-free too?
faq.answer: Swap the butter for a plant-based stick butter and use full-fat coconut milk instead of sour cream and milk.

faq.question: How far ahead can I bake these?
faq.answer: Bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store unfrosted at room temperature. Frost the day you plan to serve them.

conclusion: These cinnamon brown sugar cupcakes prove gluten-free baking can still taste like a cozy cinnamon roll. Make a batch and see how fast they disappear.
